R30 addressed affine and polynomial jets, not these rational coefficients.

Fix prime `p=6m+1 >=7`, field `F_p`, carrier `V_m=F_p[X]_{deg<m}`, and `0<=r<m`. Define

```text
h_r=(4/3)_r*r! / ((11/12)_r*(17/12)_r),  h_0=1,
W_r=(2r+1)*2^r,        S_r=(8r+13/3)*9^r*h_r.
W(f)=sum_r W_r*f_r,    S(f)=sum_r S_r*f_r.
```

Here `S_r` is **after** the exact R25 Hadamard transport from S coefficients to the free W carrier; the original W/S series, weighted outputs and their p-adic provenance remain different. Define a rational rank-jet `P(theta)=N(theta)/D(theta)` with nonzero `N,D in F_p[t]`, and `D(r)!=0` for every declared `0<=r<m`. Then `S(P(theta)f)=W(f)` for every `f in V_m` if and only if `S_r*N(r)=W_r*D(r)` for every `r`.

## Theorem A — rational operators have a growing **total degree** budget

For every prime `p=19 mod24`, put `n=deg N`, `d=deg D`. Any pole-free rational jet implementing `S(P(theta)f)=W(f)` on **every** `f in V_m` obeys

```text
max(0,m-5) <= n+d <= m-1   (the upper bound is achievable by interpolation).
```

The lower inequality holds for **every** such rational solution; the upper statement says there always exists at least one solution with `n+d<=m-1`, not that every arbitrary solution has small degree. Consequently, no fixed rational numerator/denominator degree budget independently of `p` transfers the true all-input weighted observer on arbitrarily large primes `p=19 mod24`. In fact the exact recurrence has **no nonzero rational solution as an identity in F_p(t)** for any such `p`.

**Proof.** R25 supplies `S_r !=0` for every strict index in this residue class. R30 supplies, for `R_r=W_r/S_r`,

```text
R_r/R_(r-1) = B(r)/A(r) (1<=r<m),
A(t)=216*t*(2t-1)*(3t+1)*(24t+13),
B(t)=(2t+1)*(24t-11)*(12t-1)*(12t+5).
```

Every denominator in that recurrence is a p-unit on the strict range. If `R_r=N(r)/D(r)`, clearing the *nonzero* denominators forces

```text
Q(r)=0 (1<=r<m),
Q(t)=A(t)*N(t)*D(t-1)-B(t)*N(t-1)*D(t).
```

The leading coefficients of A and B are 31104 and 6912. Shift by 1 does not change a polynomial's leading coefficient. Consequently

```text
deg Q=n+d+4,     lc(Q)=24192*lc(N)*lc(D),
24192=2^7*3^3*7 != 0 (mod p) for every p=19 mod24.
```

Thus Q is **not the zero polynomial**, yet vanishes at `m-1` distinct field elements. Root counting forces `n+d+4>=m-1`, or `n+d>=m-5`. Over the rational function field itself a hypothetical identity `A P=B P(t-1)` would make Q identically zero, contradicting the same nonzero leading coefficient. For existence at cost `m-1`, interpolate `R_r` on the m distinct residues `0,...,m-1` by its Lagrange polynomial N of degree <=m-1 and take `D=1`. This interpolation uses the **entire** m-coordinate observer; it is not a uniform fixed-order local operation. QED.

## Theorem B — the 13 mod24 weighted zero excludes every regular rational jet

For each prime `p=13 mod24` there is precisely one strict rank `r0=(p-13)/24` with `S_(r0)=0` but `W_(r0)!=0` (R25). Therefore **no rational `N/D` regular at all strict ranks**, of *any* degree, represents W by `S(P(theta)f)` for every input: applying the asserted equality to `f=X^(r0)` gives `W_(r0)=0`, contradiction. This consumes the R25 source-hole classification, but extends its explicitly declared **pole-free rational observer** scope.

A formal pole at `r0` or a regularized weight derivative is a *different operation* that needs its own additional original-index/valuation data; the vanished S scalar cannot silently be treated as an invertible coefficient.
